subject: Post-call: Pilot sizing, deployment options & pricing scenarios
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Pilot sizing, deployment options & pricing scenarios

Liam / Janelle — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and a suggested plan so we can model costs accurately for Cortex's pilot and next-phase runbook.

Summary of what I heard:
- Target: conversational assistant for support triage (avg input 40 tokens, avg response 120 tokens).
- Peak traffic: ~8 qps sustained for 2 hours/day, burst to 30 qps for short campaigns.
- Data sensitivity: PII within messages; Cortex prefers VPC connectivity and customer-side KMS for production.
- Goal: pilot for 6 weeks with measurable latency <300ms p95 and cost per resolved conversation target ~$0.02.

What I attached: redwood_tco_template.xlsx — please drop any raw QPS/throughput numbers or token totals you already track. Also attached a short one-pager of how we think about per-token vs capacity economics.

Deployment options we should model (quick asks to size each):
1) Hosted API (fastest): we price per-token + optional reserved commit (discount tiers). Good for low-to-medium sustained QPS and rapid iteration.
  - I need expected monthly total input+output token volume and tolerable p95 latency.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs/pool): predictable monthly cost, better for sustained throughput and lower marginal per-token cost at scale.
  - I need target sustained qps, percent of time at that level, and any burst patterns.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): required for regulated data + customer KMS. Higher setup & infra fees; committed contracts typical.
  - I need network egress constraints, whether you want single-tenant GPUs, and SOC2/audit timelines.

Pricing knobs I'll model for the pilot:
- Per-token price (hosted) vs committed GPU-hours (dedicated).
- Burst capacity/overage rules.
- Starter credits / pilot discount (we can apply a one-time credit to get you running).

Action items / ask from you:
- Fill the attached TCO sheet with existing/expected qps and token counts where possible (or just put rough estimates).
- Confirm whether PII requires VPC/KMS for the pilot or only for production.
- Any procurement lead times or PO templates we should be aware of.

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up on Thurs to walk the TCO with Marcus (cc'd) and sketch a draft pricing estimate. Are you available 9:30–10:00am PT?

Thanks — looking forward to modeling out realistic numbers.

Best,
Ava Chen

Looping in a quick economic framing so we have numbers to show on Thurs.

Assumptions from Liam's numbers:
- 2.5M requests over pilot -> ~400M tokens (2.5M * 160 tokens)
- Sustained 8 qps for 2 hours/day -> that's ~57k requests over those daily windows (fits their daily 60k).

Rough scenarios (ballpark, before discounts/credits):
1) Hosted (per-token):
  - Example per-token list price: $0.000015 per token (input+output) -> 400M * $0.000015 = $6,000 for pilot
  - Add: reserved-commit option (1 month) could lower to ~$0.000011/token -> ~$4,400
  - Pros: fastest start, no infra setup. Cons: VPC/KMS not in pilot unless we enable private endpoint (adds setup cost).
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pool):
  - For 8 qps sustained on medium LLM setup, estimate needing 1x reserved GPU (NVIDIA A10x/80) with autoscale buffer for bursts. Monthly reserved cost ballpark: $12–16k/month. For a 6-week pilot pro-rated ~ $18–20k.
  - If Cortex commits to 3mo, unit economics improve and marginal per-token cost drops below hosted at high sustained qps.
3) Private VPC / On-prem:
  - One-time onboarding + baseline infra: $25k–40k depending on single-tenant GPUs & network setup. Ongoing monthly infra costs similar to Dedicated but with professional services.

Pilot recommendation (quick): Start hosted with a small reserved commit + pilot credit ($4k–6k net) to validate latency/quality, run the pilot, then move to Dedicated or Private for prod when Cortex needs VPC/KMS and sustained throughput. We should build a path with a single PO that covers pilot credits and optionally converts into a reserved-commit discount if Cortex opts in.

For Thurs I'll prepare a short slide with 3-scenario numbers (hosted-per-token, hosted-with-reserve, dedicated-reserve) and a conversion worksheet. Ava — if Liam can confirm the estimated token total (or drop an exported token count in the spreadsheet) I can tighten the numbers.
